summary_paragraph: Mr. Johnson, a man with a history of systolic heart failure, coronary artery disease, type 2 diabetes, and chronic kidney disease, was admitted for acute on chronic heart failure exacerbation due to fluid overload, presenting with worsening shortness of breath and orthopnea. Despite medication adherence, dietary challenges contributed to the decompensation. He was treated with IV and oral diuretics, including a trial of metolazone, which improved fluid status but caused transient worsening of kidney function. A diuretic holiday was implemented, after which therapy was resumed successfully. His breathing improved, and he was transitioned to oral torsemide at a reduced dose. Paroxysmal atrial tachycardia was noted on ICD interrogation, prompting initiation of warfarin for stroke prevention, with INR 1.8 at discharge. A urine culture grew coagulase-negative staph, deemed contaminant. Repeat imaging ruled out pneumonia. He was discharged home with close follow-up, medication reconciliation, and instructions on weight monitoring and dietary compliance.
problems: Acute on chronic systolic (congestive) heart failure
Hypertensive chronic kidney disease with stage 1 through stage 4 chronic kidney disease, or unspecified chronic kidney disease
Atherosclerotic heart disease of native coronary artery without angina pectoris
Presence of coronary angioplasty implant and graft
